How the edge did against [sipbench](../README.md)'s scenarios at commit `3e73a74`, run 24 November 2026 04:22 UTC. The release workflow (`.github/workflows/report-card.yml`) regenerates it after every release.

| Run | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Edge on kind, through Kamailio to a 3-node `FreeswitchCluster` | 59 of 62 | 0 | 3 |
| Compose, one FreeSWITCH (M0) | 37 of 62 | 1 | 24 |

The [conformance record](../conformance/README.md) has 257 cases, 239 of which apply to this edge. Scenarios check 127 of those (53%): 60 fully and 67 in part. 112 are planned.

| `raw-legal-variants` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 14.7 | ➖ skip | Requests that are odd but legal, each of which a node must get rather than a 400 from Kamailio. New requests from a peer all go to a FreeSWITCH node, so the answer shows whose it is: a call that reaches the backend, or a refusal carrying the node's User-Agent. A method Kamailio doesn't know, and one that only looks like REGISTER, get the node's 501; escaped URIs, a semicolon in the user part, very long header values, unusual transports in lower Via values, a Date in a local time zone, odd but legal From, To and Contact URIs, several Via values in one header, escaped headers in the Request-URI and trailing spaces on the request line all reach the node (the last two are among the forms RFC 4475 allows a proxy to accept). A body of an unknown type, and an Accept that rules out SDP, get the node's 415 and 406; a MESSAGE with a binary multipart body gets the node's answer (407 here). A scheme we don't route, and an OPTIONS keepalive whose branch is the bare magic cookie, Kamailio answers itself.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-register-variants` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 0.5 | ➖ skip | REGISTERs with unusual but legal content: escaped nulls in user parts, an Authorization in a scheme nobody knows, an unknown Contact parameter, an unknown parameter inside the Contact URI, and an escaped Route header inside it. The edge has no registrar, so a REGISTER from a peer is handled like any other new request: it goes to a node, which challenges it (401). Kamailio must not refuse any of these for their syntax. Two are refused: a REGISTER whose From is an http URI gets 400 from Kamailio (its sanity check parses From and To as SIP URIs), and one whose Contact URI carries headers without <> gets 400 from the node; both are recorded as gaps in the conformance record.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |
| `raw-malformed-requests` | proxy-validation | ✅ pass | 33.6 | ➖ skip | Requests that are malformed: none may reach a node, and Kamailio must stay up. Kamailio answers 400 itself to a CSeq number too large for 32 bits, a Request-URI in <>, and a CSeq method that doesn't match the request's (for a known method and an unknown one). Its core parser drops the rest without an answer: extra separators in Via and Contact, an unterminated quoted display name, whitespace inside the Request-URI, several spaces between the request line's parts, an addr-spec with spaces, and a second To, Call-ID, Max-Forwards and CSeq. Kamailio's parser lets a malformed display name through (characters a token can't hold, outside quotes) and so does a bare From URI with a comma, but every node would discard them unanswered, so Kamailio's script answers them 400 itself. RFC 4475 would have most of these answered 400; each gap is in the conformance record.<br>*Compose: needs proxy* |

| `barge-in-vad-mode` | media | ✅ pass | 6.7 | ❌ **fail** | Which side detects the caller talking over the agent is switchable per call. With no X-Barge-In-VAD header the fleet's mode applies (livekit by default: the edge leaves detection to the agent) and the backend is told so in X-Barge-In-VAD. A caller's X-Barge-In-VAD: freeswitch turns on the edge's echo cancellation and voice detectors for that call, and the backend is told freeswitch; audio still flows both ways with no gap, so the detectors and the echo canceller sit in the path without disturbing it. A header with any other value is ignored. With the edge detecting, each start and stop of speech reaches the agent as a SIP INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) naming whose speech it was: a caller who talks over the agent's tone gives caller detections and no agent ones, an agent who talks over the caller's tone gives agent detections and no caller ones (each detector hears only its own side), and with the agent detecting the edge sends none.<br>*Compose: call edge-caller-talks: backend received 0 INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) with event=speech-started party=caller, want at least 1 (received none); call edge-caller-talks: backend received 0 INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) with event=speech-stopped party=caller, want at least 1 (received none); call edge-agent-talks: backend received 0 INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) with event=speech-started party=agent, want at least 1 (received none); call edge-agent-talks: backend received 0 INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) with event=speech-stopped party=agent, want at least 1 (received none)* |
| `barge-in-livekit` | media | ➖ skip |  | ➖ skip | The whole chain from a caller to a LiveKit agent: the edge sends an "lk" number to LiveKit SIP, which takes the caller into the agent's room (the bench's stand-in agent, sipbench lkagent) with the call's X-Barge-In-VAD as the participant's sipbench.bargeIn attribute, so the agent knows who detects the caller talking. With the edge detecting, each start and stop of the caller's speech reaches the agent as a data packet on the topic barge-in: the edge sends it to LiveKit SIP as a SIP INFO (application/x-barge-in+json) and our patched LiveKit SIP forwards the body to the room. The agent publishes no audio, so the edge hears no agent speech and sends no agent detections. With the agent detecting, the edge sends none.<br>*Kind: needs livekit*<br>*Compose: needs livekit* |

| `node-lost-mid-call` | fleet | ✅ pass | 161.2 | ➖ skip | An edge node goes dark mid-call. Ten seconds into a call the runner takes the call's node off the network for two minutes (no packet in or out, ARP included, as if it had lost power), longer than FreeSWITCH's media timeout and long enough for Kubernetes to mark the node NotReady. The rest of the fleet keeps taking calls: one placed as the node goes dark is set up within Kamailio's 5 s failover, and one placed 30 s later, once the dispatcher's probes have taken the node out, without any. When the node comes back the fleet is whole again. The call on the dark node is not checked past its first audio: until failover (M4) it is lost, and the report records its audio gap and how it ended as the baseline M4 has to beat.<br>*Compose: needs fleet, node-blackout* |
